data.claim: On main (after B-fix-contest-gaps / B-fix-renewal-overjoin) _h_resolved sets the kept lease's renewed_at = max(renewed_at, at) and never weighs the widened window against the record: A(1150,300) E(1200,300) C(150,150) D(250,50), resolve keep=D at 5000 -> contest [], displaced [A], lease D (250..5050) although A's 1150..1450 lies inside it. All 24 fold orders agree.
data.falsifier: the contest/displaced lists after resolve already holding A in a contest with D
data.mechanism: Two readings disagree: (a) re-check after widening -> A joins a contest with D, the item is blocked 'contested' again right after the operator settled it, and every resolve of a long-lapsed claim re-creates a contest with whatever took over in the gap (a resolve that cannot finish in one step). (b) widening is the modelling error: D held 250..300 and nothing until the resolution at 5000; A's claim in the gap was a legitimate TTL takeover, not a double claim. Under (b) the resolution's sign of life starts a NEW window [at, at+ttl] when the kept claim had lapsed by 'at' (keep the original claim's window on record for pairwise reads), and only claims overlapping that new window are re-checked -- normally none, since resolve released them. (c) re-check and auto-release the newly-overlapped claims as decided by the resolution: releases a claim nobody chose to release.
data.probe: python3 scratchpad probe using tests/test_lease_contest._folded over all 24 permutations, releasing lease_losers(D) then item.resolved claim=D at=5000
data.probe_output: 24x ('A','C','D','E') ([], ['A'], 'D', ['C','E']) -> contest [], displaced [A], displayed D, released C,E
data.question: Does resolve --keep X widen X's window over claims still on record without re-checking them? (B6805b48aca) And what should the window be?

data.body: Bug B6805b48aca, research R9afca028e2. resolve --keep X sets renewed_at = max(renewed_at, at): a long-lapsed X is treated as held from its claim to the resolution, and claims on record inside that gap are never re-weighed (A(1150,300) E(1200,300) C(150,150) D(250,50), keep D at 5000 -> contest [], A displaced, though A lies in D's widened 250..5050). Options: (a) re-check after widening: A joins a contest with D, the item is contested again right after it was settled, and a resolve of a lapsed claim can never finish in one step. (b) RECOMMENDED: widening is the modelling error -- when the kept claim had lapsed by the resolution's 'at', the resolution starts a new window [at, at+ttl] (the original claim's window stays what pairwise reads use) and only claims overlapping the new window are re-checked; A's claim in the gap was a legitimate takeover. (c) re-check and auto-release newly overlapped claims: releases a claim nobody chose. Regression test: the 24-permutation probe in tests/test_lease_contest.py asserting the chosen outcome. Blocked until the operator picks a model.
data.title: resolve --keep X: the kept claim's window after a resolution is weighed against the record (fixes bug B6805b48aca) -- NEEDS OPERATOR DECISION

data.body: Bug B6805b48aca, research R9afca028e2, decision D-resolve-fresh-window (operator, option b). resolve --keep X set renewed_at = max(renewed_at, at): a long-lapsed X was treated as held from its claim to the resolution, so a claim another agent made legitimately in that gap sat inside X's stretched window and was never weighed (A(1150,300) E(1200,300) C(150,150) D(250,50), keep D at 5000 -> D displayed over 250..5050 with A inside it). Now, when the kept claim had lapsed by the resolution's 'at', the displayed lease is X's claim with a fresh window [at, at+ttl] and X's original window stays on the record (displaced), so a late claim that overlapped X's real tenure is still a contest while A's takeover in the gap is not. Claims overlapping the fresh window are re-checked and join a contest with it. A claim still live at 'at' is extended as before (no gap). Records of one claim are keyed by (event, acquired_at) where its two windows could be confused: join, displace, widen, and the late-renewal 'is this the displayed lease' check. A release of X's claim ends both. Tests: the A/E/C/D repro over all 24 fold orders, a late claim inside X's original window, a claim inside the fresh window, and the release/resolve property test extended with resolutions dated after every claim.
data.title: resolve --keep on a lapsed claim starts a fresh window; only claims overlapping it are re-checked (fixes bug B6805b48aca)

evidence.note: R9afca028e2 CONFIRMED (24 fold orders: keep D at 5000 -> contest [], A displaced inside D's stretched 250..5050); operator decision D-resolve-fresh-window picks option (b).

ddflow brief --item B-fix-resolve-widened-window: decision D-resolve-fresh-window governs ddflow/core/model.py (followed); the lease-contest invariant 'a claim forgotten is a double claim nobody is told about' kept by leaving the kept claim's original window on record.

e240f62: _h_resolved -- a kept claim lapsed by 'at' (renewed_at+ttl < at) is displayed with acquired_at=renewed_at=at, its original window is displaced by that fresh window, and claims overlapping the window it now holds are re-checked (_clashing/_join); a live claim is extended as before. Records of one claim keyed by (event, acquired_at) in _join, _displace, _widen and _late_renewal's displayed-lease check, so the two windows never merge. Tests: 137 failed on the unfixed model (A/E/C/D repro x24, late claim in the real tenure x24, claim in the fresh window x24, gap renewal, fresh-renewal, the extended release/resolve property on 15/40 seeds, resolve-keeps-every x48 with its updated assertion); tests/test_lease_contest.py 458 passed after.

data.body: Bug B79c2f6e17a: P1.T1 split into sub-task P1.T1a, P1.T2 needs P1.T1 -> critical_path == ['P1.T1','P1.T2'], though T1 closes only when T1a does; longest() walks inherited_deps only.
